rule: A contract changes only by a new version. The spec, every implementer and the tests change in the same commit, and the change is recorded in decisions.jsonl. tests/run_tests.py checks that every file below carries the current marker.

contracts.what: Normalized conversation JSON and message ids (T3u, T3a, T3a2), and the same ids in Markdown markers.
tests: schema: renderer tags the version and gives every message a unique mid
schema: an unknown version is refused by seed, SSD and telemetry

contracts.what: The handoff file: front matter, sections, states, log line, and the folder's .ledger.json owner and lane settings. @2 (HO-20261101-005): random lane-coded ids (HO-LANE-YYYYMMDD-XXXX), actors with a session (lane#session), steps recorded 'for' another party. Optional touches: (paths, globs or thread URLs) for overlap warnings; readers that don't use it ignore it. @1 files (HO-YYYYMMDD-NNN, no sessions) stay readable and valid.
tests: ledger: prepared -> sent -> acknowledged -> completed, then check
ledger: a handoff from a newer contract version is refused
ledger: @2 needs a session on every actor; the owner needs none

contracts.what: Marking relayed and pasted material: a FROM: first line, FROM: ... END FROM blocks, and >""" pastes.
tests: ssd: a FROM ... END FROM block after your words is stripped from own text
seed: a FROM block inside your message is flagged as a paste, speaker stays you

contracts.what: chat-relay's reply statuses: done (explicit completion signal), unconfirmed (text stopped, no signal), pending.
tests: relay: text that stops changing without a signal is never "done"
relay: explicit ChatGPT completion -> done

contracts.what: Read-only export of a records store: manifest.json (queried sources, counts, time bounds, hashes, filters, redaction policy, exclusions, coverage gaps) and records.jsonl (one record per item, with kind, rid, source_path, source_hash, lane, actor, ts/ts_missing and evidence_class). Reads conversation@1 and handoff@1/@2; changes neither.
tests: export: message round trip from a conversation@1 capture preserves text, ids and order
export: a relayed message is marked relay with its origin, distinct from original speech
export: missing captures, hidden steps, absent timestamps and missing outputs are reported in the manifest
export: a destination inside a public or unconfirmed GitHub repository is refused

contracts.what: What the decision and challenge ledgers say is open, settled, in force or contested, decided once (tools/lifecycle.py) and shared by check_ledgers, status, export, the MCP server and the cockpit. A supersedes takes effect only from a settled line (adopted closes any earlier decision; rejected and superseded settle a proposal only and cannot retire an adopted decision); a proposed line is a proposed replacement; a resolves only from a resolved or accepted-risk line; self, forward and unknown references are problems and take no effect; more than one effective closer is a conflict, kept, not collapsed. Applicability of an adopted decision: standing ('adopted, no structured supersession found'), superseded, revoked (revokes), expired or not yet effective (effective_from/until); amends (an id or {id, clauses}) records a partial amendment. Export records gain applicability, closed_by, proposed_replacements, amended_by, conflict, transition_problems (decisions) and open, closed_by, conflict (challenges); in_force follows these rules. Adopting a proposal replaces what it proposed to replace; a closing and a revoking line on one record is a conflict; an amendment lapses with what it amends; effective dates are evaluated against the ledger's latest date by every reader; check_ledgers reports invalid transitions on earlier lines as warnings. export and mcp stay @1 with this deviation recorded in docs/lifecycle.md.
tests: lifecycle: the six review reproductions and the other fixture cases resolve as specified
lifecycle: check_ledgers refuses exactly the cases with a transition that takes no effect
lifecycle: status, export, the MCP server and the cockpit show the same open items and in-force decisions
lifecycle: a transition that takes no effect on an earlier line is a warning, so later appends still work; a new one is refused

contracts.what: Read-only static control surface over a records store: DIR/index.html (one self-contained page: Choices, Topology, Budget, Run/Drift and the other v0.4 surfaces) and DIR/cockpit.json (the data it was built from). Choices compose paste-ready ledger_append / handoff set lines and write nothing (DEC-019). Reads decisions, challenges, handoff@1/@2, threads.md and conversation@1 through the export@1 readers, plus governance/budget.jsonl; changes none of them. Deterministic; no clock is read (the newest record, the records revision and its commit and fetch times are shown, not today). @2 (HO-RK-20261105-VZH4): each choice says what it asks (the proposer's optional `ask`, else a summary labelled derived), what cites it and waits on it, its age, and whether it may be overtaken (later citations; opt-in build-time PR states); Amend and Clarify compose ledger lines (an amending adopted line; an open question challenge addressed to the proposer); Inquire copies an off-record prompt; Questions lists open questions. @3 (HO-RK-20261105-SWK5): a Pull requests surface rendering governance/pr-state.jsonl (relay-kit/prs@1): each PR's What / Why / How / Authorized verbatim with who wrote it (an agent's Author: line is tagged as not the owner's), missing sections, reviews with their family and whether one is from another family than the author, CI, and read times; PR states for the overtaken check come from that file, so --pr-state only fills gaps. --theme FILE (known colour variables and font lists only; an optional light scheme with a toggle) and --landing SURFACE. The page still fetches and writes nothing. Additive: nothing in @2 changed meaning. @4 (HO-RK-20261105-8DTW): reads the ledgers through relay-kit/lifecycle@1 (a proposal leaves Choices only when a settled line closes it; a proposed replacement is shown on its card; transitions that take no effect or conflict are listed on Review); every composed decision or challenge line carries --expect ID=STATE@HASH (and one for what a proposal replaces) so ledger_append refuses it, with what changed, once the item has moved on; the header shows the records' revision, commit time and last fetch (aged in the browser) apart from the newest record. Nothing from @3 was removed. @5 (HO-RK-20261106-NXPR; DEC-139, DEC-140): Pull requests folds each review under its card with author, family (signed, or inferred from the login via review_families or the records' .ledger.json 'actors' map, and labelled so; else unsigned), kind (review or review-style comment), verdict, time, inline-comment count, and the body verbatim as escaped paragraphs and lists (no markdown executed, URLs as text); a 'Findings: N blocking / M should-fix' line only when the body states those counts. A Status surface (11, a --landing target) renders the newest relay-kit/status@1 edition verbatim from a markdown subset, tags its author, flags it stale past --drift-days (measured from the newest record), and indexes older editions. Choices show relay-kit/decision-support@1 notes per item, one block per author in reading order (independent authors, the owner, then the coordinator lane), latest per author with history, and 'no decision-support note yet' otherwise; the ledger mechanics (what each action does) sit behind a 'how the ledger records this' disclosure. Decision, challenge and decision-support text is rendered with its structure: (1)…(n) enumerations, numbered or dashed lines and line breaks become lists and paragraphs, escaped, never markdown. cockpit.json gains status, decision_support, choices[].support, reviews' kind/body/family_source/findings/comments, and counts.status_editions/support_notes/choices_without_support. Nothing from @4 was removed.

cockpit: Inquire is off the record: no command, no ledger line, only a prompt naming the item

cockpit: an agent-written PR is tagged as not written by the owner; one with no Author line says so

cockpit: reviews fold under the card with author, family or unsigned, kind, verdict, time and the body as escaped paragraphs; Findings only as stated
cockpit: a family taken from the login (the records' actors map or review_families) is marked inferred; a Reviewer: signature is marked signed

contracts.what: governance/pr-state.jsonl, append-only, written by relay-kit prs at build time from GitHub (gh CLI or a token): a 'pr' line when a pull request's state changed since its last line (repo, number, url, title, state open|closed|merged, draft, author, author_line from the body's Author: line, times, base, head, reviews [{by, verdict, at, signed, stated}], ci {state success|failure|pending|none, failing}, body_sections {what, why, how, authorized} verbatim with HTML comments removed, missing, truncated) and a 'fetch' line per run (ts, via, repos, ok, failed, since_days, prs_seen, appended). Repositories from handoffs/.ledger.json 'repos' or --repo. The one GitHub reader for pull requests: the Cockpit and other readers read the file. @2 (HO-RK-20261105-TXRM step 1): pull requests are read through tools/github.py, the kit's read-only client for pull-request reads (GET only; pagination; retries with backoff; rate-limit waits or refusal with the reset time; one fetch per path per run; optional ETag cache). A pr line gains `unread` (reviews or ci that couldn't be read: missing is not zero; ci state 'unknown'); the fetch line gains `coverage` per repository (what was asked, listed, more_available, re-read open PRs, PRs read, partial reads), `revisions` (default branch and pushed_at) and `client` (requests, retries, waits, cache hits, rate limit left, first/last request time). @1 lines stay readable. @3 (HO-RK-20261106-NXPR, DEC-139): each review carries id, kind 'review', its body verbatim (cut at 4000 characters, truncated: true) and comments (its inline-comment count; the inline text stays on GitHub); issue comments that are reviews in all but type (first non-empty line opening with Review / Execution review / Reviewer, or a verdict stated in the opening words) are recorded as reviews with kind 'comment', verdict null and the same fields; unread may say 'comments'. One more read per PR (issue comments) and one per PR with reviews (inline comments). @1 and @2 lines stay readable; a PR whose reviews gained bodies gets one new line on the first @3 run, an unchanged PR none.
tests: prs: body sections are kept verbatim; missing and comment-only sections are listed as missing
prs: an unchanged PR appends no new line; a changed one appends one, and every run appends a fetch line
prs: a failing repository is recorded in the fetch line and the others are still read
prs: it writes only governance/pr-state.jsonl and never rewrites a line
prs: CI state from check runs and statuses; reviews keep the verdict stated in their body
prs: repositories come from .ledger.json repos or --repo; anything not OWNER/NAME is refused
prs: a PR last recorded open is read again however old, so a closed one never stays open
prs: appending to a file without a final newline doesn't join two lines
github: pages walks pages until the limit or a short page, and says whether more were available
github: network errors and 5xx are retried with backoff; other errors and exhausted retries are refused with the status
github: a rate limit waits for the reset when it is short, and is refused with the reset time when it isn't
github: a path is fetched once per run; with a cache folder an unchanged resource is revalidated by its ETag
github: the gh transport only ever sends GET, and parses status and headers from its output
prs: what was asked for and what came back is recorded per repository; unreadable reviews or CI are unread, not none
prs: a PR that can't be read again is a partial read, not a failed repository; an unread part keeps its last value and adds no line
prs: review bodies are recorded verbatim (cut at 4000, flagged), with inline-comment counts; review-style issue comments join as kind comment
prs: review-style comments that can't be read are unread, keep their last value, and never read as none

contracts.what: A hand-written status edition: status/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<edition>.md in the records store, with front matter date, edition, author, covers (and contract) and the four H2 sections Accomplishments / Road bumps / Status / Next steps, in a markdown subset (ATX headings, lists, bold, italic, inline code, horizontal rules, fenced code shown as text; links shown as text; HTML comments removed; anything else plain text). Editions are added, never edited or rewritten; the newest is the latest date, then morning < midday < noon < afternoon < evening < night, then other names alphabetically. The Cockpit renders it as written; `relay-kit edition new` scaffolds one and `check` reports what doesn't fit. Adopted from the pilot form kairos/status@0, which has the same fields.
tests: status: `relay-kit edition new` scaffolds the front matter and four headings and never overwrites; `check` reports what doesn't fit
cockpit: Status renders the newest edition verbatim from the markdown subset (escaped; links as text), indexes older ones, and can be the landing

contracts.what: governance/decision-support.jsonl, append-only: one line per authored decision-support note, {id, item (the DEC/CH/HO id it is about), author (actor with session), at, contract, changes_if_accepted, unchanged, counterfactual, can_wait, depends, recommendation}, all free text written by the author named; the latest line per (item, author) is current and earlier ones are its history. Nothing in it is generated. Readers show one block per author in a reading order (independent authors, the owner, then the coordinator lane) and rank nothing. Lines of the pilot form kairos/decision-support@0 (same fields) are read as @1.
tests: cockpit: decision-support notes render per item, one block per author, independent authors before the coordinator, latest per author with history; mechanics folded

contracts.what: Read-only MCP server over a records store, JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, protocol revisions 2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25 (any other gets -32022 with the supported list): the tool names and arguments, relaykit:// resource URIs, the result envelope (schema, evidence_class as in export@1, provenance 'read from <path> at records sha256:<hash>', content_level, notice) and the --content metadata policy. No tool writes to the records (DEC-019).
tests: mcp: initialize handshake, tools/list and ping over stdio, for each supported protocol version
mcp: a 2026-07-28 or unknown protocol version gets -32022 with the supported list, never a silent fallback
mcp: every read tool answers with evidence_class and a provenance line naming the records hash
mcp: with --content metadata no tool or resource returns record text, and text filters are refused
mcp: read tools change nothing in the records, and instruction-like record text isn't acted on
mcp: malformed JSON-RPC gets a proper error and the server keeps serving
